text:
incident-bot: Pager: routing.loop.detected — high rate of cross-region fallback churn between us-east, us-west, eu (routing.loop.pingflap). 5xx spike on prod-facing endpoints. Auto-suppressed after 3 mins but recurring. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/alerts/12345
ryan: ack — oncall ryan here, looking. getting logs and topology.
olivia: saw customer error reports ~10:58 UTC, some timeouts then 502s. rough impact ~2-3% global TPS.
paul: rolling health-check counts look weird — probes failing in a pattern: us-east marks eu unhealthy -> traffic reroutes to us-west -> us-west marks us-east unhealthy -> loops back.
jen: pinging the routing policy service now. quick check: which fallback policy is active? could be aggressive 'closest-healthy' w/ zero cooldown.
mike: policy snapshot from control plane: `fallback_policy: { mode: "latency-pref", cooldown_s: 0, prefer_variant: auto }` — that's the problem, cooldown 0 + prefer_variant auto can flip variants/regions quickly.
emily: also seeing KV cache churn on the model serving nodes after failover, increasing memory pressure -> some OOMs on smaller nodes.
ryan: mitigation plan: 1) add cooldown to fallback policy (30s), 2) temporarily set prefer_variant to stable-small for user-facing routes, 3) disable cross-region fast-failover. doing 1 now.
jen: recommend bump to 60s if possible. 30s may still oscillate.
paul: agree, 60s safer. while we change policy, should we pause the health probe aggressiveness? probe interval is 5s with 2 failures -> down. bump to interval 15s and failures 3 to reduce sensitivity.
mike: applying policy patch in control plane: `PATCH /v1/routing/policies/region-smart-1 {"fallback_policy": {"cooldown_s": 60, "prefer_variant": "stable-small", "allow_cross_region_failover": false}}` — submitted, waiting for propagate.
incident-bot: Deploy event recorded: routing-policy/region-smart-1 PATCH by mike at 1718004427.
ryan: changing health probe config on probe-manager: `set probe interval=15s failures=3` and restarting probe-agent on us-east/us-west/eu. doing now.
emily: restarted probe-agent on us-east and us-west. eu still draining traffic, restart queued.
olivia: customer-impact update: error rate dropping from 2.8% -> 1.1% after changes (10m window). some customers still see intermittent 502s.
paul: note: a secondary issue — model variant auto-selection was switching variants during failovers, causing KV cache flushes. setting prefer_variant to stable-small should mitigate.
jen: recommendation for next 30m: monitor cross-region reroute metrics, error rates per-customer, and model node memory OOMs. assign someone to runbook/annotation.
ryan: assigning sretask: @emily will own monitoring + postmortem steps, @paul owns routing policy follow-up, @jen owns runbook updates.
emily: noted. I’ve pinned dashboard: https://console.redwood/dashboards/routing-loop-1718004321 and added alert threshold of >0.5% 5xx for 5m to trigger high-priority.
mike: control plane shows policy patched and propagated to 98% of edge proxies by 1718004490. still 2% lagging (old config).
paul: I’m going to force push config to remaining proxies now: `for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app=edge-proxy -o name); do kubectl exec $pod -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/apply-config -d @policy.json; done` — running.
emily: OOMs subsiding on smaller model nodes. cache hit rate improving.
olivia: customer reports calming down; CS desk updated. no VIP customers on outage at the moment.
jen: quick note: root cause hypothesis: overly aggressive fallback policy (cooldown 0) combined with sensitive health probes (5s, 2 failures) plus auto-variant selection caused cascading flaps between regions.
ryan: agreed. immediate mitigations done. next actions: 1) keep cooldown 60s for 2 hours, 2) revert prefer_variant to auto after stability validation 24h, 3) update runbook to include explicit probe/timeout knobs and a deploy-time policy guard.
paul: will open follow-up ticket: RFC-ROUTING-349 with rollback/backout test matrix.
emily: will prepare post-incident notes and customer impact summary (est. 45m total elevated errors window, peak 2.8% affected).
mike: suggest adding policy validation: CI job to detect cooldown=0 or allow_cross_region_failover=true for global routes.
jen: +1. also add a canary for variant-switching during route failover in the model serving tests.
ryan: anyone see any remaining 5xx spikes?
emily: last spike at 1718004999 — small blip, now stable.
olivia: closing the page with note: mitigation in place, monitoring for 1hr. will reopen if we see >0.5% 5xx for 5m.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated — monitoring (1718005123). Pager cleared.
ryan: thanks team. postmortem owner: emily. tag me if you need help.
emily: will draft and share within 48h. will include timeline, root cause, and code snippets for the hotfix.
jen: adding checklist: policy default cooldown >=30s, probe defaults interval >=10s for cross-region, require approval for prefer_variant:auto on global routes.
paul: filing customer-facing note draft for CS.
ryan: done here. clear. great job. :thumbsup:
